text:
Alex: FYI CI microbench on PR 21799 failed threshold for `batcher_small` (latency +12%). marking as rollout blocker :exclamation:
CI-bot: build: https://ci.internal/redwood/21799/artifacts 
CI-bot: perf-diff: batcher_small median latency 18.6ms -> 20.9ms (+12.4%), p99 56ms -> 68ms (+21%), test: infra/microbench/batcher_small 
Mira: ugh, that % jump looks like kernel selection flip under small batches. did we change autoselect heuristics in the merge? :thinking_face:
Sam: I ran the same microbench locally with `--seed=42 --runs=200` and saw the same median bump. repro command: `./tools/microbench --bench=batcher_small --kernel=autoselect --quant=auto --runs=200`
Cheng: any telemetry around KV cache hit rate during the run? if kvcache hit drops we can see tail latency spike.
Sam: attaching short flame slice (reduced):
```
flamegraph snippet:
  70%    gpu::kernel_dispatch
   40%   -> runtime::batcher::wait_for_coalescer
   30%   -> runtime::kernel_selector::choose_quantized_path
```
Looks like more time spent in kernel selection logic and wait paths.
Mira: interesting — the PR enabled quantized fallback for certain op combos and bumped the autoselect cost table (commit 98f3a2). maybe under small seqlen it prefers a quant path that causes extra kernel negotiation overhead.
Taylor: I pulled the ci artifact and diffed the perf logs. kvcache hit rate dropped from 89% -> 62% during the run window. stacktrace shows more cache evictions triggered by `prefetch_window` shift.
Alex: so two leads: (A) kernel autoselect chooses a quantized variant causing extra negotiation/warmup, (B) prefetch/window change made kvcache thrash. either can explain latency.
Cheng: can we bisect to the single commit? try reverting 98f3a2 (quant fallback) in CI and rerun microbench. if that fixes, we ship a hotfix revert.
Mira: I'll queue a bisect job: revert quant fallback commit, keep allocator/prefetch commits. starting job now: https://ci.internal/redwood/21799/bisect/1 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
CI-bot: bisect job queued, job id 21799-bisect-01. will post results when done.
Sam: meanwhile I added a focused test locally toggling `kvcache.prefetch_window` from 8 -> 4 and it restores hitrate and latency back to baseline. snippet: `kvcache_hit=87% lat=18.8ms`
Taylor: if bisect confirms, patch plan: revert quant-fallback commit (risk low), and follow up with a targeted kernel-selector optimization to avoid negotiation on small batches.
Alex: agree. if bisect doesn't point to quant fallback, we escalate to full bisect across prefetch/kv/selector commits. owner: Mira (bisect) + Sam (local repro & perf graphs) + Cheng (kvcache telemetry). aim: revert or hotfix by EOD. :eyes:
Mira: update: bisect CI finished, revert of 98f3a2 -> microbench back to baseline. landing an emergency revert PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/21805 :white_check_mark:
Sam: verified post-revert CI perf artifacts show median 18.5ms, p99 57ms. marking this thread resolved for the rollout blocker.
Cheng: will open follow-up issue to rethink quant fallback handshake cost and add microbench coverage for small-batch autoselect path. assigning to runtime team.
Alex: thanks everyone. we'll hold the release until we ship a patched autoselect that avoids negotiation churn on small batches.
Taylor: note for postmortem: add golden metric for kvcache hit rate to microbench harness to catch this earlier.
CI-bot: thread closed by Alex at 6135793280
